articleTitle: Transformer-less Switched-Capacitor Inverter for PV Application
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study proposes a single-phase switched-capacitor (SC) topology that eliminates the need for a transformer and incorporates a shared ground. The topology utilizes eleven switches, one diode, and three capacitors to generate a nine-level waveform. The key attributes of the proposed design include zero leakage current (LC), voltage boosting capability, reduced voltage stress, and self-balancing of capacitor voltage. Furthermore, there is no need for extra balancing circuits or sensors to ensure the equilibrium of capacitor voltages. A comprehensive examination of the circuit description and operating principle has also been conducted. Through a concise comparison, the proposed topology has been shown to outperform existing alternatives in terms of component count, voltage stress, and gain. The utilization of the simulation environment ensures the accuracy of the theoretical concept.

articleTitle: PSO and WOA Algorithm Based Optimal Control for Photovoltaic Solar System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved photovoltaic solar system controller and the MPPT (maximum power point tracking from the photovoltaic (PV) module. It is retrieved using the P&O (perturb and observe) technique since the solar power production varies on the ambient factors, such as irradiance and atmospheric temperature. Particle Swarm optimization (PSO), Whale optimization algorithm (WOA) and standard proportional and integral (PI) controllers are some of the controllers that are used to get the most power from the PV system. The effectiveness of conventional and ideal controllers is assessed and contrasted in the MATLAB-Simulink environment. The outcome demonstrates that when compared to traditional PI controllers, PSO-based and WOA-based optimal controllers, in which WOA-based optimal controller produce better output outcomes.

articleTitle: Design and Energy Dissipation Analysis of Full-Adder for Low Power Applications Using Reversible Logic Gates
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Low-power architectures are gaining traction in applications ranging from IoT to quantum computing. Traditional combinational logic circuits suffer from information loss and energy waste. Reversible computing mitigates this issue by sustaining input bits in the output. Adders are vital in arithmetic and logic units, impacting processor performance. Reversibility design principles offer promising ultra-low power solutions. We propose an energy-tolerant, low-power reversible full adder with optimized energy loss, reduced ancillae, garbage outputs, and quantum cost. This advancement holds potential for quantum computing and other energy-efficient applications. The transistor count per adder circuit is also reduced compared with existing architectures that exist in the literature.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator for Resilient Control of Microgrid Under Cyber Attack
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Increasing penetration of power electronic interfaced renewable energy resources in microgrid leads to reduced system inertia, which in turn results into a microgrid vulnerable to load change and leads to frequency instability. Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) incorporates synthetic inertia to microgrid, which replicates conventional power plant properties like rotational mass and oscillation damping to reduce load frequency transients. In this paper, we introduce a VSG that in addition to providing extra inertia in a low inertia microgrid, also makes the system resilient against extreme conditions such as cyber-attack. PID controller is extensively used to represent primary, secondary controllers and rotor of synchronous generator in VSG. Achieving accurate tuning of VSG /PID controller parameters may be challenging. In this paper the parameters are tuned by Zeigler-Nicholas (Z-N) technique which is successful even for systems with uncertain mathematical models and works on the system's transient response and hence is a natural choice of tuning controller parameters. In recent times, the vulnerability of power system under cyber-attack has become a very important aspect of research. This paper establishes that the VSG introduced in the microgrid is effective in improving the resiliency of the system under different cyber-attacks. Therefore, the present paper proposes a VSG that fulfils the purpose of improvement of performance of a low inertia microgrid for load frequency control in event of sudden load change, variation in renewable generation and also works effectively to protect the system under cyber-attack.

articleTitle: A Multiband Patch Antenna Using Meander Line for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this proposed article, a simple monopole patch antenna with meander line for multiband operation is introduced. Using meander line into the patch antenna design the overall performance of antenna gives better simulated results. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are (24×20×1.6) mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which is compact in size and can be easily combined with other devices. This proposed antenna is implemented on FR-4 substrate with height of 1.6mm having dielectric constant 4.4 and loss tangent value is 0.02. The proposed design is simulated by CadFeko Software tool. The designed antenna is resonant at four frequencies 6.52 GHz, 9.22 GHz, 11.95 GHz and 13.74 GHz which covers C, X and Ku bands. The response of designed multiband antenna is showed in terms of return loss (S11), efficiency, Voltage SWR, 2-D radiation pattern, 3-D radiation pattern, current and gain.

articleTitle: Lung Cancer Detection and Classification using Transfer Learning with Pre-trained VGG19 Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: It is possible to diagnose and identify a variety of illnesses with the use of high-quality figures obtained from medical equipment. However, obtaining and storing these kinds of photos may be quite costly, and diagnosing a patient might take a long time. Artificial intelligence (AI) solutions for automatic diagnosis may play a major role in addressing the challenges of time and cost. The categorization of medical images may be effectively solved by pre-trained deep learning models. Lung cancer continues to be a widespread and serious type of cancer on a global scale. Timely and precise identification is crucial for successful treatment and enhanced patient results. This study presents a novel approach to the identification and categorization of lung cancer by using transfer learning via a VGG19 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that has been trained beforehand. Our work harnesses the power of transfer learning by leveraging the VGG 19 architecture, provides the basis for lung cancer diagnosis, having been pre-trained on a large dataset. Our carefully curated dataset encompasses over 14600 diverse lung images, covering benign, malignant, and normal cases, providing the model with a rich source of information. The model demonstrated outstanding performance metrics, achieving a training accuracy of 99.68%, 98.11% for validation accuracy and 97.93% for test accuracy. Such high accuracy holds great promise for expediting and improving the diagnostic capabilities of healthcare professionals. By leveraging Transfer Learning from VGG19, our model demonstrates adaptability to diverse medical imaging tasks, making it a valuable tool for real-world clinical applications.

articleTitle: Investigation on Performance of PMU Assisted Distance Relays in Power Grids with High Penetration of MPPT Driven Solar Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Sources in power grids across the globe are undergoing transition from conventional synchronous generators to power electronic converter interfaced renewable energy sources. A significant proportion of such energy sources is solar farms. The maximum power extraction is of elevated interest for the better utilization of sources and to harness maximum profit. However, the inherent diurnal variability and rapid variation of solar insolation in presence of moving clouds causes maximum power point to drift across operating regions. The MPPT algorithm under such scenarios is found to inject interharmonics into the power grid. The impact of these injections on power system protection systems, especially on the distance relay operation, is not well reported in literature. This paper investigates in detail the impact of interharmonics injected by solar farms operating under MPPT on distance relays. Case studies are conducted based on the real-world data available from literature.

articleTitle: A Robust $\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$ Filter Design for State of Charge Estimation of Li-Ion Battery with Time-varying Parameters: Application to Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a novel state of charge (SOC) estimation filter criteria for the lithium-ion battery (LIB) dynamics with time varying parameters using <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$</tex> approach. By utilizing a Lyapunov-Krasovskii Functional (LKF) approach and Linear Matrix Inequality (LMI) technique, a new robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{L}_{2}-\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$</tex> filter algorithm has been exploited for the feasibility of LIBs, which optimize the performance of the battery dynamics. Finally, a simulation example is presented to show the effectiveness and benefits of the developed filtering design approach.

articleTitle: Differential Protection Challenges in Auto Transformers with Tertiary Delta Windings - A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Autotransformers are vital components in power systems, ensuring the secure interconnection of Extra High Voltage (EHV) and High Voltage (HV) networks. They demand reliable protection systems due to their role in transferring substantial energy. This paper addresses the challenges of differential protection in autotransformers with tertiary delta windings, particularly when delta winding current is unmeasured. The paper discusses the principles of differential protection based on ampere-turn balance and the algorithms employed by modern numerical relays. It explores the impact of zero sequence compensation on protection sensitivity and phase identification and underscores the importance of measuring delta winding current. Two real-world cases illustrate the challenges faced in autotransformer differential protection, where the relay detected current in all three phases, making fault identification difficult. By calculating the differential currents, the paper provides insights into the relay's behavior in these scenarios, emphasizing the need for delta winding current measurement to enhance protection selectivity.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar Energy Capture: Exploring Absorber Layer Thickness in Carbon-Nitrate-PSK Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research work is focused on the expedition of a SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/Carbon-Nitrate-PSK/Spiro-OMeTAD solar cell by the variation in the thickness of the absorber layer. The Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) software is used for the simulation of the device. The structure of the device is already published work, with SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is considered as the electron transport layer (ETL), Spiro-OMeTAD is considered as the hole transport layer (HTL), and the Carbon-Nitrate-PSK as the absorber or active layer. The aim is to optimized the photons absorption from the sunlight. The research is examining the effect of the absorber layer's thickness variation from 600 nm to 1100 nm on the performance of the device. The optimized PV parameters of the Carbon-Nitrate-PSK based cells are - FF: 81.85%, PCE: 20.89%, VOC: 1.047V and JSC: 24.355mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Reliability Assessment of DC Microgrid Using Markov Model
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In terms of grid safety and economics, reliability is an essential component of power system design and operation. Distributed generation (DG) sources connected through power electronic converters (PECs) are the integral part of the DC microgrids. As a result, the reliability of the DC microgrid (MG) will be impacted by their failure characteristics. Therefore, the traditional methods of assessing reliability, may provide misleading data for taking the decisions for planning and operation of DC MGs. This study presents work that uses a Markov model to access the reliability of DC MG systems. Modelling the microgrid using the connectivity between the source and the loads and computing the system parameters is performed using a Markov model. A test system is considered to demonstrate the impact of faults and component failures on the reliability of DC MGs.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit for Inverter fed Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper describes a method to determine the instantaneous input current, output power, input power factor and efficiency of sine PWM inverter fed induction motor using equivalent circuit. This method can be used for inverter fed induction motor with any PWM technique. The possible variation in all the parameters of induction motor equivalent circuit is also investigated and is compared with experimental results.

articleTitle: Amplitude Death in Two Coupled Van der Pol Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In the study of coupled non-linear oscillators' dynamic behavior, amplitude death is an important phenomenon. It displays both oscillation suppression and amplitude. Generally speaking, amplitude death is an issue that has received somewhat less attention from academics than synchronization and anti-synchronization, which are likewise results of linked non-linear systems. In many systems, amplitude death is a useful technique for suppressing unwanted oscillations. Combining the repulsive and attractive couplings will result in the amplitude death.In the current study, we use Lyapunov stability analysis to compute adequate coupling gain for amplitude death in a system of two Van der Pol oscillators. Through numerical simulations, the result is verified.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of Tri-State Boost Converter for Solar PV Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Expanding energy request and natural issues are the real worries to propel research in the field of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) and its applications. Convectional sources of energy are quickly exhausting and the expense of energy is increasing and accordingly photovoltaic (PV) system is a standout amongst the most encouraging choices because of contamination free, disseminated all through the earth. PV cells are interconnected in a suitable way to obtain PV module and PV array which is used to produce electric power contingent on the climatic environments. Power electronic converters (PEC) goes about as an interface between input PV system and output to enhance the power flow. Conventionally, boost converter is inured to increase the voltage obtained from the solar PV system. Instability is a major issue in the boost converter due to the existence of right-hand plane (RHP) zero. In this paper, A novel topology tri-state boost converter is utilized to analyze the stability of the system and frequency response analysis using bode plot is carried out accordingly to judge the presentation of the system. Tri-state boost converter is implemented in closed loop using proportional integral (PI) controller as well as fuzzy logic controller. The investigation is done in MATLAB/SIMULINK and results including PV voltage, response of the converter and inductor current are related between predictable boost and tri-state converts.

articleTitle: Unlocking Emotions Through Heat: Facial Emotion Recognition via Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Facial emotion recognition involves the analysis of facial expressions to identify and classify human emotions. As there is a relationship between facial temperature changes and emotions, this study focuses on facial emotion recognition using thermal imaging. The primary goal of this work is to enhance the efficiency, robustness, and accuracy of emotion recognition systems to improve human-computer interaction, mental health monitoring, personalized education, marketing effectiveness, and security. The proposed Convolution Neural Network (CNN) architecture is designed to recognize human emotions by classifying facial images into six distinct categories (happiness, sadness, anger, fear, disgust, and surprise). With an average detection accuracy of 0.9857, the proposed model showcases its effectiveness in emotion prediction. The findings indicate that our proposed system outperforms YOLOv5 and YOLOv5-NMS models across all emotions, showcasing superior results.

articleTitle: Passivity-Based Observer Design for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Charge Estimation with Parameter Uncertainties for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The motive of this paper is to explore the state of charge (SOC) observer design for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) with time-varying parameter uncertainties for electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) using passivity theory for the first time. Based on the construction of the Lyapunov-Krosovkii functional (LKF) and linear matrix inequality (LMI) technique a novel robust state observer criterion is developed for the solvability of LIBs in terms of equivalent circuit mathematical model (ECMM) in the sense that SOC performance, which ensures the optimum performance of LIBs for EV applications. Finally, a fascinating simulation example is demonstrated to show the usefulness and benefits of the proposed approach, and this was demonstrated through a comparison of our results over existing methods in the literature.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Mitigating Cross-Regulation in SIDO Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Monitoring and control of Power Electronic Converters (PEC) to avoid the catastrophic failures and undesirable malfunctioning conditions; becomes an essential criterion to be satisfied in the present industrial needs. This paper is one among the kind to discuss the monitoring and mitigating the cross-regulation occurring in multiport converter entities. In this paper, Single Input Dual Output (SIDO) type Buck converter is proposed with Coupled Inductor (CI) topology including a Machine Learning Model (MLM). Pertaining to the MLM, Logistic Regression Analysis (LRA) with SoftMax function is employed to predict the occurrence of cross-regulation during the load dynamics and to estimate the intensity of the same. The proposed CI-SIDO Buck converter is designed for an input of 48V, delivering 12V with a capability of 75Watts and 24V with a capability of 125 Watts. The converter under consideration is controlled by a dual PI controller supported with Type-II compensator. The proposed technology is developed in a Hardware-In-Loop (HIL) platform on the dSPACE-MicrolabBox-DS1202. The major outcomes of the paper are investigating the occurrence of cross-regulation, self-adaptation in mitigating the magnitude of deregulated voltage, different load dynamics and its respective case studies using bode-plot.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Control of Non-Ideal SEPIC Converters Using Leverrier's Algorithm and PI Controller Considering Parasitic Elements
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents the modelling of a fourth-order dc-dc converter, introduces a simple systematic approach to calculate the resolvent matrix in order to obtain the small signal transfer function of the dc-dc converter and the implementation of a PI controller to synchronize its output voltage with input voltage and load disturbances. A SEPIC (Single Ended Primary Inductance Converter) dc-dc converter with uncoupled inductors rated 100- Watt power has been designed specifically for battery charging applications. In certain applications, a SEPIC converter is used where the input voltage can be either higher or lower than the required output voltage. A SEPIC consists of two inductors and two capacitors for this reason, its mathematical model is of the fourth-order differential equations. The dynamic model of the converter is obtained through the State Space Averaging (SSA) technique in the presence of non-idealities specially source resistance which has been overlooked by researchers. Leverrier's Algorithm-based approach is applied here to calculate the resolvent matrix. The tuning of the PI controller parameter is done using the Ziegler-Nichols method. At last, the derived dynamic model and calculated PI controller parameters are verified through MATLAB Simulation.

articleTitle: Optimal Coordination of DOCRs Utilizing Disparate Relay Characteristics in a Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The article discusses about Directional Overcurrent Relays (DOCRs) coordination for the distribution system with DGs integrated. Disparate DOCR characteristic is utilized to mitigate the protection issue in all mode of grid operation. The fault current level in the system varies with the change in network condition. Consequently, conventional protection scheme fails to operate and hence optimal relay coordination of (DOCR) arises. In this manuscript, the impact of utilizing different DOCR characteristics has been investigated for mitigating this problem. Extensive research studies have been conducted for estimating the impact of change in operating mode of microgrid on protection coordination. In this work initially the microgrid was designed with 6 bus distribution system. Consequently, the impact on total relay operating time and Coordination Time Interval (CTI) for different relay characteristic has been observed for Grid-connected as well as Islanded modes of Microgrid operation. Subsequently, the key parameters are calculated in terms of CTI, operating time, TMS, PS etc. Further, percentage reduction in the sum of operating time of all the relays with mix curves is obtained to be 22.41 % for grid connected mode and 9.79% for islanded mode with NI characteristic.

articleTitle: Inspecting Transfer Learning Models for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Astonishingly, 285 million individuals of the global diabetic population, exhibit sign of diabetic retinopathy. It has become a prominent global health challenge arising as a complication of diabetes. Diabetic Retinopathy damages the retina's delicate blood vessels leading to blurred vision, dark spots in vision, retinal detachment and ultimately vision loss. To address this concern, we implemented a study to explore the possibilities for automated DR detection using advanced deep learning techniques. We assessed four models namely, EfficientNet-B5, ResNet152V2, EfficientNet-B6 and MobileNetV2, on the Asia Pacific Tele-Ophthalmology Society (APTOS) dataset of retinal images. MobileNetV2 emerged as a top-performing model, closely followed by EfficientNet-B6, with the potential to revolutionize diabetic retinopathy diagnosis and reduce the risk of vision loss. These findings contribute to the field of medical image analysis, offering promise for enhanced early detection of diabetic retinopathy.

articleTitle: Optimizing PV Parameters in CH3NH3PbI3 Based Cell Through Device Modeling
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Perovskite materials have developed a lot of attention in the photovoltaic (PV) industry owing to its exceptional properties like high power conversion efficiency (PCE), tunable bandgaps, and low cost. Electron transport layers (ETL) and hole transport layers (HTL) are used to improve charge carrier mobility in perovskite solar cells. Choosing the best ETL and HTL is of the utmost importance for optimal perovskite-based solar cell design. Choosing the best ETL and HTL is critical for optimal perovskite-based solar cell design. We used silver thiocyanate (AgSCN) as the HTL in the PCBM/CH3NH3PbI3/AgSCN solar cell in this investigation. We examined the cumulative impact of thickness and bulk defect density (BDD) on several PV parameters of the cell to optimize its performance. The results demonstrated the following PV parameters: open circuit voltage (Voc) of 0.962 V, short-circuit current (Jsc) of 19.743 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, fill factor (FF) of 86.68%, and power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 16.47%. The research shows that having a thicker layer for improved photon absorption is helpful for improved cell PV performance. It is also critical to keep the defect density low in order to minimize charge carrier recombination.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Low Inertia Power System due to Increasing Penetration of Solar PV Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Due to decreased cost, improved comparative efficiency, government subsidies, and technical development, the solar PV industries are thus seeing stratospheric expansion on a global scale. Although there are numerous functional, technical, and financial difficulties, as solar PV integration into the electrical grid is not plain and simple. The issues of grid integration for PV systems were discussed in this paper. In this study, IEEE 9 bus system has been modified to examine the effects of large-scale solar photovoltaic penetration on the overall system response. The findings imply that a reduction in the overall system inertia will result from solar photovoltaic generation contributing to several disturbances. As a result, disruptions and contingency events become more likely to occur in the system.

Author Keywords: Rate of Change of Frequency etc

articleTitle: Traveling Wave Based Fault Location and Fault Classification Technique for Distribution Networks with High Renewable Penetration
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Distribution systems have become more complex with the increased penetration of renewable energy sources. In standard operational scenarios, the increased proliferation of distributed generation technologies, including photovoltaic systems, electrical interfaces, and power electronic-equipped battery storage, may result in bidirectional power flows. In the event of a short circuit, this configuration could yield minimal fault current. These can affect the protection system of the distribution system. This paper discusses detecting the fault location and identifying the fault type by using extracted features of traveling wave after the fault occurred in distribution networks with high renewable penetration. The research is based on the XGBoost model trained by features obtained through zero sequence current and 3 phase currents from the PSCAD simulation.

articleTitle: Automating Load Banks for Enhanced Testing Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Load banks are crucial tools for testing power sources, dissipating electrical energy as heat. However, they often present challenges like heat emissions, remote operation limitations, and the need for manual coordination. This IEEE paper introduces an innovative solution: the automation of load banks. Our approach leverages the ESP32 microcontroller, relay control modules, and cloud connectivity to streamline load bank operations. This automation reduces manual intervention, enables dynamic load control, and facilitates real-time monitoring, making load banks more adaptable to changing requirements. By exploring the system's architecture and load control algorithm, this paper presents a practical solution for modernizing load bank operations in industrial settings. This advancement enhances testing efficiency and responsiveness, aligning load banks with the evolving demands of industry stakeholders.

articleTitle: CMOS Based Temperature Sensing Via Change in Threshold Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The design and simulation of MOS-based temperature sensors in the 65nm technology node using Cadence Virtuoso are shown in this work. By running MOSFETs in the sub-threshold range, the sensors exhibited extremely low power consumption. A diode-connected NMOS is used as the sensing element, and an interfacing circuit is used for signal conditioning and amplification. The sensor operates at 1.2 V supply voltage, uses just 96 μW of power, and has sensitivity of 0.177 mV/°C. The sensing temperature range of the sensor is between -50°C and 200°C.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dual Branch Equal Gain Combining Over Correlated Lognormal Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In wireless communication systems, the performance of the transmission link is significantly affected due to small- and large-scale fading effects. Log normal fading most accurately models these effects over large distances. Equal gain diversity combining or (EGC) is an effective technique for mitigating fading effects and improving the signal quality at the receiver. This study investigates the performance of EGC on dual correlated log normal fading channels. Lognormal summations and integrals are difficult to resolve into evaluable closed forms, which makes analysis of lognormal fading channels a task of magnanimous proportions. This text combats the above mathematical difficulty by deriving expressions for the average output Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and the Amount of Fading (AF), as these parameters turn out to be easier and more intuitive for the purpose of understanding combiner performance for the considered wireless system. A comprehensive analysis for the entire range of positive correlation values is made, with performance comparison between EGC, Selection Combining (SC) and Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC) on both performance parameters considered.

articleTitle: Microorganism Detection using Single-Shot Multibox Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The advent of microorganism detection has proved invariably useful to the scientific community, especially considering the recent pandemics across human history. There is a continuous rise in the occurrence of pandemics across the world which has made the need for innovative and swift detection methodologies more important. The current study proposes the usage of Single-Shot Multibox Detector (SSD) for detecting microorganisms which is unexplored till date. The proposed model utilizes EMDS-6 Dataset which has 840 images spanning 21 distinct microbe classes, with 40 images per class. The chosen model, SSD MobileNet V2 FPNLite 320×320 from the TensorFlow 2 model zoo has demonstrated more than satisfying results for performance with good accuracy and precision in detecting microbes. The results show the robustness and versatility of this SSD-based approach. The discussion of the results is also done along with the future scope of the current project.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Power-Sharing and Stability Using PSO-Tuned PSS for Inverter-Based Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper outlines the development of a power system stabilizer (PSS) for enhancing the power-sharing and stability of a droop-controlled inverter-coupled microgrids. In conventional power systems, the power system stabilizer is employed to dampen low-frequency oscillations and ameliorate stability. In Inverter-coupled generating source-based microgrid the droop controller plays a vital role in maintaining systems stability. Increasing the droop coefficient will improve power-sharing, but the stability of the microgrid has an adverse effect with the introduction of oscillations in system frequency. To address this issue, a PSS is proposed. In this study, the PSS parameters are tuned utilizing the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The integral squared error of the frequency of generating sources is adopted as an objective function to fine-tune both the time constants of a lead compensator and the gain of the PSS. The efficacy of the proposed PSS is showcased through time-domain simulations and eigenvalue analysis. The outcomes are then juxtaposed with those obtained from a PSS based on a traditional approach, considering different droop gain values. The PSO-based PSS outperforms the conventional technique and needs fewer calculations by achieving faster power-sharing and enhancing the dampening of low-frequency modes.

articleTitle: A Controller Hardware-in-the-Loop Based Approach for Testing Distribution System Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Protection plays a vital role in power systems as it ensures the effective management of abnormalities across all hierarchy levels of power system, including generation, transmission, and distribution. Failure to implement appropriate protective measures can result in cascaded outages, leading to complete blackouts or partial outages in power supply. The focus of the present study is centered around modeling and analyzing the protection system performance applied to a 5-bus distribution system. The testing of protection and control mechanism is significant and Controller hardware- in-the-loop (C-HIL) is a significant platform to test protection operation under varied faults and network conditions to ensure enhanced reliability of the protection system. In this study, the Typhoon HIL real-time simulator is employed to construct a virtual environment that accurately mirrors the behavior of a power system. In addition to simulation, the study places significant emphasis on the validation of digital protection systems through the use of C-HIL testing. Through this validation process, the study ensures testing of the digital protection systems function as intended so that they can effectively respond to abnormal conditions within the distribution system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Transformer less UPS in Addition with Reactive Power Compensation for Industrial Application
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: An Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) is essential in providing reliable and efficient power to sensitive loads such as hospital life-saving infrastructure, telecommunication systems, and airplane computers. Regardless of the grid conditions, the UPS output remains closer to sinusoidal, making it more stable and reliable. Some other benefits of a UPS include minimum transient reaction time from grid mode to battery mode, almost unity power factor, high reliability, low cost, less weight, high efficiency, and good steady-state response time. The proposed UPS topology includes a bidirectional converter, a DC battery, a single-phase H-Bridge inverter, and an RL load with a diode bridge rectifier that acts as a non-linear load. The bidirectional converter helps to provide adjustable DC link voltage to supply the inverter and correction of power factor. During the power ON condition, the inverter functions as a reactive power compensator device, thereby enhancing the overall power factor of the system. In case of power CUT condition, the inverter provides sufficient power to the essential load, and the bi-directional converter functions as a buck converter during the ON condition of the supply and as a boost converter during the power cut condition of the supply. This configuration reduces the voltage drop across the transmission lines and improves the overall power factor of the system.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Mode Selection and Control of Multiport DC-DC Converters In PV-Battery Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of a multi-port DC-DC converter in hybrid Renewable Energy Source (RES) applications. In the hybrid source integrations, the challenging role for the controller is to choose the appropriate source based on its availability; thus, performing a promising job for the energy management system. In that way, the mode selection still remains a complicated concept for the design engineers due to the fact that involves in detailed learning and prediction algorithm. This paper is one among the kind in designing a Machine Learning (ML) algorithm for mode selection and control of hybrid RES system. In this article, an extendable DC-DC converter is considered with multi-port capability on the source side with battery back-up. The operation of the converter in different modes will be decided by the ML algorithm. The performance analysis of the proposed technique is conducted in Hardware-In-Loop fashion, where the ML logic is developed in Matlab and integrated with experimental hardware using dSPACE-MicroLabBox. The mode selection and operational features with the proposed technique are validated with simulation and experimental results as well.

articleTitle: Enhanced Image Quantization Through Hybrid Sine Cosine Optimization and K-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The need for quantization of color images arises because of limitations of image display and hardcopy, data storage, and data transmission devices. Many of the current methods for color simplification in images don't provide the best results. This can lead to noticeable color changes and the appearance of false outlines, especially when trying to represent images with a small set of colors. This paper describes a new approach to finding the optimal solutions of the color image quantization problem using a Sine Cosine Optimization (SCO) algorithm. The nature and the difficulty of the problem and its formulation are discussed. Then, the SCO algorithm is presented, and the representation of the problem with this method is explained. The effect of theparameters such as the Sine and Cosine phase updating rulesand population size on the quality of solutions is studied. Solutions obtained with the SCO algorithm are compared with those of heuristics and the K-means clustering algorithm, demonstrating the superior quality of the results achieved with the SCO algorithm.

articleTitle: ANN-Based (PI + PIλ) Controller for LFC Analysis in 2-Area Deregulated Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents an ANN-based (PI + PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>) controller for LFC (Load Frequency Control) in the 2-area connected power system, aiming to simplify frequency regulation. The controller uses an OVPL (Opposition-learning-based Volleyball Premier League) algorithm for parameter excellent tuning, enhancing its effectiveness in analyzing the integrated gas-nuclear turbine and thermal-hydro power systems. The study uses an artificial neural network to modify the parameters of a (PI + PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>) controller, revealing that an ANN-based controller exceeds an OVPL-based controller concerning performance as well as stability, based on comparisons.

articleTitle: SAM based Computational Analysis of Root Mean Square Error for SPES Using LR, RF & ARIMA Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Renewable energy is crucial in addressing various global challenges like climate change, global warming, human development index, etc. To address these challenges, wind and solar energy are the mature technologies to harness green power. Integrating machine learning into the renewable energy sector can lead to more efficient, reliable, and sustainable energy systems. The work proposed for the solar photovoltaic energy system. The solar photovoltaic system of 500kW AC is simulated in the System Advisor Model (SAM). The data for annual energy generation is fetched to form the dataset. This dataset from SAM contains the hourly energy generation data for a particular year. The comparative analysis is proposed after mining the dataset. The machine learning algorithms are Linear Regression, Random Forest and ARIMA. To evaluate the performance of these algorithms, the statistical measure, namely Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), was used. The comparative analysis shows the effectiveness of the proposed work and its dataset for the machine learning algorithms.

articleTitle: Design of a T-S Fuzzy Regulator Using PDC and NAE Approach and Integral-Optimal Sliding Mode Control for Current-Controlled Electromagnetic Levitation System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this article, the Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) regulators and integral sliding mode with optimal control-based controllers are proposed for the current-controlled electromagnetic levitation system (CC-EMLS). The Takagi-Sugeno regulator is designed using the parallel distributed compensator (PDC) and negative absolute eigenvalue (NAE) for achieving the set-point of the levitating steel ball. The Takagi-Sugeno regulator is not suitable for systems with significant uncertainties and cannot handle large-scale models because in the process of gain calculation it requires many linear models. A sliding mode controller (SMC) is therefore developed to deal with the uncertainties in the system model. The chattering effect is observed in the sliding mode control technique. The integral sliding mode control (ISM) provides the chatter-free control input that protects the system from becoming unstable, and optimal control in the ISMC provides the necessary action for tracking the desired position. The effectiveness of the proposed control techniques is compared by adding the disturbance to the levitating object mass. The designed controllers are robust enough to cater to external disturbances and parameter variations. The transient and steady-state performances of the system are analyzed for the designed controllers in terms of integral errors such as ISE, IAE, ITSE, and ITAE. Simulation experiments presented in the article validate the performance claim and robustness of the proposed controller for the magnetic levitation system.

articleTitle: A Modified Viterbi Decoder Architecture for Hardware Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Viterbi decoders play an important role in modern wireless communication systems to decode convolutionally encoded information. Hardware design of Viterbi decoders have been explored widely with a focus on achieving low area, power and delay. In this work an attempt has been made to achieve the same by combining the methodologies available in literature for modifying the Survivor Memory Unit (SMU) and Add Compare Select (ACS) unit of a Viterbi decoder. Here, the modifications on the ACS unit using T-algorithm with pre-computation together with retiming has been combined with the modification on the SMU using the pre-trace back approach. Both of these modifications that have been reported independently in literature, have been combined in this work. The architecture incorporating the modifications in the ACS unit and SMU together leads to a design with a reduced area and power of 21.21 % and 49.1 % respectively, while at the same time increasing the maximum operating frequency by 67.7 %. A comprehensive verification environment for the unit has also been developed using system Verilog layered test bench.

articleTitle: SOC and SOE Estimation in Lithium-ion Batteries for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries have indeed become the battery technology of choice for electric vehicle(EV) manufacturers for several compelling reasons such as high energy density, low weight, fast charging and many more. Accurate monitoring of battery states is crucial for optimizing the energy storage management system of electric vehicles. Battery state monitoring helps ensure efficient operation, prolonged battery life, and enhance safety. In this paper, we have proposed a simple method of combined state of charge (SOC) and state of energy (SOE) estimation. In this work, we begin with modeling of Li-ion cell using the 2RC model, then Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (AEKF) for SOC estimation and Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for SOE estimation which is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink. Lastly, the simulation results demonstrate the algorithm's precision and suitability.

articleTitle: Magnetic Coupling Spiral-Square Coil Mutual Inductance Evaluation for Interoperable Conditions with Different Misalignments
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, an investigative method is used to evaluate the mutual inductance between two spiral square coils arranged on the transmitter and receiver sides of a flat planar surface. The investigation of mutual inductance between the coils is performed considering all potential spatial variations, including both lateral and angular misalignments. In empirical contexts, it has been noted that spiral square coils demonstrate a higher capacity to withstand planar misalignments in comparison to circular coils. Moreover, spiral square coils exhibit a higher coupling coefficient, which holds considerable significance. Although there exists a substantial body of literature on the investigation methods for mutual inductance (MI) in two spiral circular coils, as well as a recently enhanced Neumann's method, there has been a dearth of studies focused on MI calculation methods specifically tailored for spiral square coils. The validation of Neumann's technique for calculating mutual inductance is achieved by employing finite element analysis and an experimental configuration. A comparison is made between Neumann's method, a finite-element model, and the Simulink solution, which are three different ways to figure out mutual inductance. The results of the three techniques demonstrate a significant level of agreement in MATLAB/SIMULINK across all situations.

articleTitle: Harmonic Reduction Strategies for EV Charging in Power Systems Using Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) globally and the large-scale integration of EV chargers into the distribution grid have led to significant concerns about the quality of power and current in the system. An EV needs a charging station for battery charging, the harmonics thus introduced owes to frequent use of power electronics devices. In order to compensate the harmonics, and reduce the reactive power needed for EV charging stations, a shunt active harmonic filter (SAHF) has been introduced. This paper implements dq method-based control of SAHF and a highly effective control loop for generating reference current. A PWM switching technique for 3L-NPC inver-ter has been used in the proposed work. The presented paper includes design aspects of power circuit, controller parameters of a SAPF, and system performance for the specified parameters. The efficacy of the designed parameters of SAPF for reactive power and harmonic compensation has been shown using the simulation results. Based on these results, it can be deduced that the compensation process based only on sensing line currents, is instantaneous and the implement is easy. The THD of the source current in this proposed work is well below 5%, the limit as per the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Hybrid Smart Microgrid System Modelling, Design and Control Using an Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The usage of electrical networks which are not connected to the electrical grid allows for the provision of electrical energy to remote places. We refer to these electrical networks as standalone microgrid systems. The design and control for a freestanding microgrid system based on Solar Photo Voltaic (PV) panel's, Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) and Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) which forms a Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES) are discussed in this study. When the Solar PV panel's output exceeds the load requirements, it is used to recharge the battery system and is drawn from the batteries when the PV panels' output is not sufficient to satisfy the maximum demand. The proposed Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller safeguards the battery banks charging and discharging conditions. Irrespective of the battery's State of Charge (SOC), an ANFIS controller performs under normal operating configurations with typical settings as 20%< SOC< 80%. A special triggering command signal is sent and it turns-off the Solar PV panel's and wind turbine system when SOC hits 80%. If SOC falls below 20% the inverter turns off and disconnected from the system. Each case is supervised by the controller using MATLAB/Simulation Software.

articleTitle: Assessment of Voltage Unbalance Factor to Evaluate its Effect on Three Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Firstly, this paper provides the fundamental understanding of voltage unbalanced (VU) and its adverse impacts on three phase induction motors (3-ΦM). Then, the voltage unbalanced factor (VUF), provided by IEC standard, has been considered to quantify the impacts of VU on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\phi$</tex> IM. The various parameters of performance, such as the copper loss, the input power factor and the efficiency for a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\phi$</tex> IM are computed for the fixed and different values of VUF. It is revealed that the VUF alone is not a sufficient index to assess the impacts of VU as there can be innumerous voltage sets possible for a fixed value of VUF. Therefore, in this work it is asserted that, one more index, representing the condition of VU, is highly desirable along with VUF to get accurate impacts of VU on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\phi$</tex> IM. Finally, the various indices to quantify the condition of VU have also been incorporated in discussion. Also, the performance parameters of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\phi$</tex> IM are estimated with these indices to show the impacts of condition of VU on the performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\phi$</tex> IM.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Battery Charging Utilizing High Gain Luo Converter with Power Factor Correction
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study focuses on enhancing the performance of electric vehicle (EV) battery chargers by reducing stress on the devices used in power factor correction (PFC). It achieves this by incorporating a high step-up gain Luo converter in conjunction with a flyback converter. The high-gain Luo converter is advantageous because it operates with a shorter duty cycle which is due to a switched inductor at the input. This leads to reduced conduction losses and better overall charger efficiency when compared to conventional Luo converters. To regulate the battery's current, a flyback converter is utilized, functioning in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) to uphold a consistent voltage-constant current mode. The design of the high-gain converter and the flyback converter involves the use of fewer sensors and a smaller magnetic volume, resulting in cost and size savings. The system undergoes testing to assess the enhanced power quality (PQ) performance of the charger under steady and quickly changing line voltages. Compared to other voltage-lift-type Luo converters documented in literature, this converter demonstrates reduced strain on devices, fewer parts, and enhanced efficiency. Moreover, a closed-loop control system using cascaded proportional-integral (PI) controllers in the flyback converter ensures more precise and controlled output. These findings are validated through MATLAB SIMULINK simulations of the converter's performance.

articleTitle: Position Control of Electrohydraulic Actuator Using Triangular Position Signal in Open Loop Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electrohydraulic actuation systems are widely used in a variety of industries, including robotics, manufacturing, mining, agriculture, and vehicle manufacturing. Some industries, such as agriculture and mining, require low or medium control accuracy, which can be achieved with an open-loop control strategy, whereas others, such as robotics and manufacturing, require higher control accuracy, which can be achieved with an advanced closed-loop control strategy. In this paper, an electrohydraulic actuation system with a novel experimental setup is used to control the actuator position using an open-loop control strategy. For this purpose, a triangular signal with an amplitude of 100 mm and frequencies of 0.05 Hz, 0.10 Hz, and 0.20 Hz is fed into the system, and the response of the actuator position is analyzed. To process the signals, the National instrument (NI) controller was used in conjunction with the LabVIEW program. Experiment results show that position tracking error is lowest, error evaluation parameter correlation coefficient is highest, and mean absolute error and root mean square error are lowest at lower frequencies (0.05 Hz) compared to higher frequencies (0.10 Hz and 0.20 Hz).

articleTitle: Reduction of Data Leakage Trojans in Modulation Scheme of TDMA using Encoding and Decoding
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Hardware Trojans have the ability to steal user passwords and other vital information. The Data Encryption Standard (DES) encoding and decoding modulation method of time division multiplexing is dealt in this work. The sequential Randomized Encoding of Combinational Logic (RECORD) system is less secure than the Time Division multiplexing (TDM) version of the proposed system. This work concentrates on the combination of TDM with DES and its hardware realization. The proposed system is used to protect the circuits from any malicious third-party when the Trojans are aware of entire data. This method has been simulated in Verilog and synthesized using Xilinx ISE. The results highlight 37% reduction in power and 12% improvement in delay. Significant reduction in area is also obtained.

articleTitle: An IoT-Based Sustainable Automation System for the Garments Industry in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Readymade Garments sector accelerates Bangladesh's development. The “Made in Bangladesh” brand has also helped to boost Bangladesh's reputation and brand recognition on a global scale. Despite its limited resources, the country has maintained a 6% annual GDP growth rate while attaining extraordinary social and human development. On the other hand, the phrase “Internet of Things” (IoT) refers to a broad concept that can be summarized as an ecosystem of intelligent gadgets equipped with networks, sensors, and processing tools. IoT is a new technological platform that enables the many objects in our environment to connect via sensors and the Internet to improve our quality of life. Manufacturing and the industrial sector, agriculture, the health sector, smart cities, security, and emergency services, to name a few. IoT implementation in the garment sector would open a new door to growth in production and worker safety. Implementing home automation and safety systems in the garment sector will help in production and ensure the safety of the workers. The suggested IoT -based sustainable automation system for the Bangladeshi garments sector is efficient, eco-friendly, secure, reliable, and user-friendly. The system's user-friendly interface makes it straightforward to use and manage. The Bangladeshi garments industry's IoT -based sustainable automation system is a comprehensive and integrated solution that addresses the industry's primary difficulties and provides a sustainable and viable future.

articleTitle: Solar Powered MPPT Buck-Boost Converter Using Adaptive ML Algorithm and Smart Controller For DC Fast Charging Application
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The utilization of photovoltaic (PV) systems for generating clean electricity has surged, yet their efficiency remains a concern. Researchers seek to enhance efficacy and extract optimum energy from PV panels through Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) inverters. These inverters rely on algorithms to identify the panel's Maximum PowerPoint (MPP). Simultaneously, the electric vehicle (EV) market experiences rapid growth due to incentives and eco-consciousness, necessitating swift charging stations. Traditional grid-based stations strain resources and exacerbate carbon footprints. This research highlights the promising prospects of establishing a sustainable and efficient DC EV charging infrastructure that leverages renewable energy resources. Our approach involves a Solar Powered MPPT Buck-Boost Converter, incorporating an adaptive machine learning (ML) algorithm and an intelligent controller designed specifically for high-speed DC charging applications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Grid Connected PV Array System Using Conventional and Artificial Neural Network Algorithm for Maximum Power Point Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper discusses the performance analysis of boost converter implemented with maximum power point tracking for solar photovoltaic array connected to three phase grid through voltage source converter. Maximum power point tracking is operated with two different methods i.e., Perturb and observation algorithm and feed forward neural network based Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm for variable irradiation conditions and constant temperature. Efficiency of boost converter in compared using both the algorithms thereby reducing the peak overshoot in the output power of boost converter. Artificial Neural Network is trained in a way that it improves the efficiency of the boost converter and reduces the peak overshoot in the output power. Output of the boost converter is fed to the voltage source inverter through DC link capacitor which later injected into the three-phase grid through coupling inductor. The configuration is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and results are compared for given algorithms.

articleTitle: Prediction of Behavioral Movement of Cattle Using Accelerometer and Gyro Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Through the observation of individual animal behavior, precision technologies are growing in the context of livestock farming to enhance management techniques and the health and well-being of cattle [1]–[3]. Numerous priority areas can be addressed by consistently gathering data on cattle behavior. The study was conducted to predict the behavioral pattern of cattle using a self-developed prototype model. This study confirmed that the prototype model, i.e., i) a Bluetooth-based cattle node with a neck collar, ii) a low-cost networked software architecture, and iii) a processing algorithm, may enhance livestock management. The low-power Bluetooth protocols provide a dependable data transfer module between the gateway and the node linked to the cow. This low-cost device might be valuable for quick and real-time implementations. A comparison study was made between annotated data and AI-ML algorithms, which showed a significant outcome. So, in this work, an advanced node-based health monitoring module is presented to correctly predict the behavioral parameters of individual cattle, which may help to predict health status far in advance.

articleTitle: Synchro Phasor-Based Fault Analysis for Smart Grid Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: It is possible to facilitate recovery, restore the system, and reduce the length of the outage by accurately identifying the distribution system fault. Since the D.G. is increasingly being connected to the distribution network, the traditional fault identification techniques are no longer suitable for the potential power distribution network. As such, fault analysis in a weak, imbalanced, multisource distribution system is difficult. To quickly identify issues with power distribution systems, this study proposes phasor measurement-based fault analysis. To analyze three phases to ground faults near the distribution feeder and generator, we employ synchro phasor technology (P.M.U.) in the MATLAB/Simulink environment. Additionally, disturbance recorders and PMUs are used for comparative analysis. The results demonstrate how effectively PMU lowers the maximum fault current and detects variations in voltage and current. In addition, several current grid-related problems are discussed in this paper, along with innovative fault-prediction and smart grid monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of High Frequency Inverters for Charging Electric Vehicles Using Spiral Shape Transmitter and Receiver Coils
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) Principle is used in this paper to provide a complete design approach for transferring power to Electric Vehicles (EVS). To transfer the power to EVS the IPT is divided into four categories, DC-AC converter, High-frequency inverter, compensation circuit, magnetic coupling, and AC-DC converter. In order to determine the effectiveness of power transfer between the coils,self-inductance of the coils, mutual inductance of the coils, and coupling coefficient, magnetic coupling is used. With the help of high-frequency switching of the inverter, the size of the converter can be reduced significantly. A 3D Modeling of the coils is done by using Finite Element Method (FEM) with ANSYS Maxwell Electromagnetic Simulation. At 1 MHz supply frequency and a power output of 500W both the inverter parameter vaules are simulated and the results are compared.From the ANSYS Maxwell Elecromagnetic simulation the different parameters of coils are calculated and simulation were performed using PSIM Simulation software and the parameters of inverters were Calculated.From the comparision of PSIM results of both the high-frequency inverters the voltage stress on the switch,current flowing through the switch and input current of EF2 invetrer has better performances than the E inverter.

articleTitle: Optimizing HEV Performance with Fuzzy Logic-Based PID Gain Tuning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper focuses on optimizing the performance of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) through an integrated approach of fuzzy logic-based PID gain tuning. The paper examines a broad range of factors that influence the system's operation, considering the dynamics of the engine, drivetrain, rotational wheel, and the applied load. For handling the optimal performance of HEVs, a unique approach is introduced. This approach utilizes fuzzy logic to fine-tune gains for proportional integral derivative (PID) controllers, aiming to enhance their efficiency. The proposed method aims to achieve an optimal balance between acceleration, speed, and range of travel while improving controller quality and response. The findings suggest that the proposed approach has the potential to enhance the performance of HEVs, and the approach outperforms existing control techniques.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Digital Stethoscope
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research explores the fusion of cardiac auscultation and phonocardiography (PCG) to enhance cardiac acoustic analysis. Traditional stethoscopes face limitations, including the need for expertise to discern abnormalities based solely on auditory information and the challenge of isolating heart sounds from background noise. We introduce a robust hardware and software framework for signal acquisition and processing, effectively reducing noise and enabling signal playback. The hardware incorporates an omnidirectional Electret Condenser Microphone, signal conditioning with AD620 and IC741, and a second-order bandpass filter for noise reduction. The Python-based software enables real-time signal recording, playback, and parameter computation. The heart sounds were acquired for 10 subjects using the fabricated chest piece. The recordings spanned a duration of one minute, and subsequently, sounds were played back, displaying both the waveform and the heart rate of the measured signal on the application screen, allowing for visual analysis. The heart rate obtained from our measurements was validated by cross-referencing it with the heart rate data derived from a patient monitoring system. Validation demonstrates accuracy comparable to clinical monitoring systems with a minimal acceptable variation. This standalone device holds great potential for healthcare, improving cardiac diagnostics' precision. Future work aims to integrate wireless capabilities, ensuring data security and ethical compliance.

articleTitle: Image Sharpening and Edge Detection using Modified Non-scalar Adder Model
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In the domain of image processing, the demand for efficient computational tools has led to the introduction of a non-scalar adder, which operates on input sequences based on the principles of stochastic computing. In this paper a Non-scalar adder driven by a control signal ‘P’ influencing its behavior is introduced. The key to this approach is the behavior of a stochastic number generator (SNG), which produces random and independent sequences. This work employs a modular architecture, facilitating scalability to different bit widths and the integration within more complex designs. The architecture is designed in Verilog using Xilinx ISE, and with minimized counter iterations, both delay and power consumption are significantly reduced. The practicality of the modified adder illustrated through its successful implementation in two critical areas: image sharpening and edge detection. Efficiency over other architectures is illustrated through MATLAB assessments with modified stochastic adder using image metrics such as SSIM and PSNR.

articleTitle: Design and Eigen Mode Analysis of Flexible Two-Beam Piezoelectric Biomechanical Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The energy generated by the physiological activities inside the human body gets wasted. To harvest this energy, a flexible piezoelectric biomechanical energy harvester (BEH) is designed using Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) as a flexible substrate and zinc oxide (ZnO) as the piezoelectric material. The structure consists of squared-shaped seismic mass and rectangular-shaped beams. The designed BEH can be attached as a band on any part of the human body for the harvesting of energy. The resonance frequency of the BEH is obtained using eigen-mode analysis and also analytically compared.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Dual-Active-Bridge Isolated DC-DC Converter Using DPS Modulation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Dual-Phase-Shift (DPS) modulation can improve the efficiency of insulated dual-directional DC-DC converter in comparison with the classical extended phase shift and single-phase shift control approach. This study investigates maximum efficiency and the power flow at various phase shift angle. Furthermore, investigate the switching behavior of insulated dual-directional DC-DC converter operating in double phase shift control is presented. The double-phase-shift modulation provides two adjustable parameters: the inner phase shift and the outer phase shift angles. It enables precise control over power flow and voltage regulation across the load, thereby enhancing the effective operation of the dual active bridge (DAB) converter. The utilization of a proportional-integral (PI) controller is employed to effectively supervise the output voltage and attain enhanced efficiency. The simulation of converter model in dual-phase-shift modulation is performed using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Integrating Heterogeneous Modalities for Comprehensive Facial Analysis: The Heteroface Database
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Heterogeneous Face Recognition (HFR) is gradually gaining importance in various domains including biometrics and cognitive studies. Classical methods are being replaced by deep learning techniques as a means to handle varied face modalities. The paper highlights the importance of HFR and introduces a face database that incorporates diversities in spectra, illumination, and formats (viz. photograph-sketch, longitudinal, 2D-3D). The role of deep learning methods has been discussed, and its advantages over the limitations of traditional methods have been emphasized. A comprehensive real-world HFR database, such as the one presented in the paper, will likely aid algorithm development, enriched by a neural network-based curation technique that enhances diversity by excluding similar instances. The paper underscores the role of deep learning techniques in tackling the challenges in the field of HFR and presents the database as a significant contribution to advances in HFR research and application.

articleTitle: Estimation of Respiratory Rate from Photoplethysmogram Signal Using Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Respiratory Rate (RR) abnormality is often an early indicator of critical illness. Reliable estimation of RR continuously from other physiological signals is an active area of research. Direct measurement of RR can be done by measuring oronasal airflow. However, this is an uncomfortable process for the patient. Hence, conventional approaches use the electrocardiogram (ECG) signal to analyze respiratory sinus arrhythmia. Photoplethysmogram (PPG) waveform analysis provides an alternate, non-invasive method of estimation, which is suitable for patients of all ages and health conditions. In this work, various techniques available in the literature regarding RR estimation from the PPG waveform have been studied. A methodology based on Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT) is proposed for Multi-Resolution Analysis (MRA) to provide the RR estimate. Comparison of the proposed technique with the existing algorithms demonstrates better accuracy for estimating RR.

articleTitle: The Control of Three-Phase Squirrel Cage Induction Motor by Indirect Field Oriented Control for E-Mobility
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper introduces the utilization of Indirect Field-Oriented Control (IFOC) in the context of induction motor control for electric mobility (e-mobility) applications. IFOC enables precise and rapid regulation of both speed and torque in induction motors. It is a widely employed strategy in electric vehicle (EV) applications. The study in this paper investigates the behavior of an IFOC-based induction motor in an EV using MATLAB simulations. Various operational scenarios of the EV, including start-up, reverse motion, sudden load application, abrupt load removal, acceleration, and deceleration, are analyzed. The simulation employs the actual parameters of an 80Hz, 5-horsepower (HP) induction motor powered by a pulse-width modulation (PWM) inverter. The performance of the IFOC control strategy for the induction motor drive is evaluated within the context of the New York City Cycle (NYCC) drive cycle.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Logic Based Energy Management for solar PV- Battery DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The rapidly growing energy demand is being achieved by renewable energy sources. However intermittent nature of the latter's supply poses significant difficulties for grid operators. In order to counteract these sporadic sources, a battery storage system (BSS) might be connected and thus enabling the construction of a DC microgrid. In this work, solar PV is integrated with a battery and the load requirement is met by the controller keeping the voltage constant. The maximum power point tracking (MPPT) of the solar PV is obtained using the fuzzy logic control (FLC). The FLC is found to efficiently track the the maximum power from the PV panel with the variation in irradiance and change in temperature. The simulation outcomes verify the PV system's performance when integrated with a BSS under standard test conditions.

articleTitle: Nearest Charging Station Identification for EV Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: As the call for electric cars (EVs) continues to surge, making sure efficient access to charging infrastructure will become paramount for encouraging their large adoption. The research addresses the urgent undertaking of optimising EV charging infrastructure by means of predicting EV charging requirements and recommending the nearest charging stations based totally on the car's charging functionality. The work goal is to expand a predictive approach that anticipates EV charging requirements and guides users to the most suitable charging stations. The approach utilizes number of object mastering algorithms, which include Decision Tree Regression, K-Nearest Neighbours Regression, and Support Vector Regression, trained on real-local charging station records from Bangalore. These techniques are designed to estimate charging points at various geographic locations, empowering EV customers to make informed choices based on their instant charging requirements. The research demonstrates the software of each set of rules in exactly predicting charging points and identifying the most suitable charging stations.
