Beyond Bangalore, the proposed technique can be adapted to benefit other cities and regions, contributing to sustainable transportation, and expediting the transition to electric mobility.

articleTitle: Intelligent Simulation-Based Training System for Harvester Operators
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A human operator still remains a critical member in any of numerous man-machine systems, who eventually determines the effectiveness of a whole system. Improvement of operator training quality in the learning process may be considered as the shortest path to productivity enhancement. The paper deals with modern approaches to operator training. Today, development of simulation-based training systems is an essential trend in the professional training of operators for technological, transport and information systems for various use. Along distinct and well-known advantages, training simulators have some drawbacks including such as a limited number of simulation scenarios of the operating environment, difficulties in individualization of a training program. We have proposed an approach mitigating the effect of the above-mentioned drawbacks due to artificial intelligence technologies. The proposed intelligent simulation-based training system ensures individualization of an operator training process based on their performance. The use of genetic algorithms enhances the variability of a simulated environment due to combination of its parameters. The proposed structure of a multi-user system makes it possible to train operators in the common simulated environment.

articleTitle: Dual Active Bridge Converter for Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure in Dual-Load Scenarios Achieving Zero Voltage Switching
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper introduces a modified Dual Active Bridge (DAB) topology combined with an LLC resonant converter for bidirectional power transfer and multiple output voltage capabilities, focusing on its application within Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure. This converter, featuring a two-stage power conversion system, offers significant advantages of high-power applications, including high efficiency, reduced voltage stress, cost-effectiveness, and the distinct Zero Voltage Switching (ZVS) property, setting it apart from isolated and non-isolated DC-DC converters. The paper delves into a detailed analysis of the converter, elucidating its operational principles, soft-switching behaviour, steady-state characteristics, output attributes, and control mechanisms. A simulation involving a dual active proposed topology with a power rating of 50 kilowatts has been conducted utilizing the MATLAB/Simulink software platform, and the resultant findings have been duly observed and documented.

articleTitle: Combined Substitution-Box Based AES Algorithm for Low Power and High Speed Crypto-Coder System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: With the demand for efficient and secure data communication increasing rapidly, crypto-coding that integrates cryptography and error control coding has become an essential part of wireless communication systems. This work deals with the design of a high speed and low power crypto-coder that uses, an Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) with an optimized Substitution - box (S-box), and a convolution encoder and a Viterbi decoder as the error control module. This design is aimed towards addressing challenges faced in the traditional implementation of low power and high speed AES architectures. It is seen that the use of the optimized AES algorithm results in 81% and 5% reduction in the power consumed and the area occupied by the crypto-coder respectively. Also, the maximum speed of operation of the crypto-coder increases by a factor of 2.5, thus lending credibility as a low power and high speed implementation.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Configuration of Devices in Mott Insulator-Based Memory Technologies
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Semiconductor RAM and Flash technology, are renowned for their utilization in cutting-edge SRAMs and solid-state drives, unequivocally reign supreme in the vast realm of volatile and non-volatile memory markets. However, it is important to note that the current technology of these devices has certain limitations when it comes to downscaling. This particular constraint may potentially hinder its progress in the foreseeable future. Resistive random-access memory (ReRAM), Magnetic random-access memory (MRAM), and Phase-change random access memory (PCRAM) have emerged as captivating alternatives that hold promise in mitigating the limitations associated with Flash memory. In contrast to these other possibilities, ReRAMs stand out as an extremely attractive alternative due to their incredibly straightforward architecture and highly promising memory characteristics. Mott materials, renowned for their remarkable insulator to metal transition (IMT) capabilities in response to various stimuli such as temperature, tension, or electrical signals, have garnered significant attention in the realm of ReRAM research.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Methodology for PV Array
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) array is one of the most important renewable energy resources, as the power generation from PV contributes significantly to the system load among renewable power generation. Further, the energy generation is free of pollution and cost, as it generates power from abundant sunlight using the photovoltaic effect. Though there are various factors, such as variations in sunlight irradiance, sunlight hours, atmosphere temperature, etc., that affect the energy generation in PV, the fault in the PV array is one of the crucial factors that affects it severely. Each fault in the PV array has its own distinct characteristics. These characteristics may be detected using the various methods proposed. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of protection methods implemented for detecting PV array faults. It discusses the features and limitations of each protection methodology elaborately. It also describes the causes of each fault and its characteristics in detail.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Photovoltaic-Thermoelectric Generator Hybrid Model Using Fresnel Lens
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive simulation of a Photovoltaic (PV) and Thermoelectric Generator (TEG) hybrid system, considering configurations with and without a Fresnel lens for different solar concentrations. The simulation, conducted using MATLAB/SIMULINK, covers a solar concentration (sun) range from 2 to 10 suns for low concentration, 12 to 20 suns for moderate concentration, and 0.2 to 1 as the conventional radiation range. The chosen light spectrum is obtained using a Fresnel lens and by varying its distance from the modules. The PV module is made up of amorphous Silicon (a-Si), and the TEG module is made up of Bismuth telluride (Bi2Te3). The results show that including a Fresnel lens to concentrate solar radiation significantly enhances the generated power and efficiency of both the hybrid and individual setups compared to the conventional system without a Fresnel lens. The results show that the hybrid system produced a power of 4.89W, 1.74W, and0.124 W at 20, 10, and 1 sun, respectively, and an efficiency of 13.32%, 8.9 % and 5.84% at 20, 10, and 1 sun, thus indicating a substantial enhancement in power and efficiency using the Fresnel lens.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Analysis of Clustering Propensity of Model Parameters of Voltammetric System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work reports a comprehensive study of the clustering ability of parameters of the recently developed models of the voltammetric (E-Tongue) system. The E-Tongue setup used in this work has been designed and used earlier for quality analysis of black tea samples. In this work, the parameters of the models are treated as features of the tea samples and they are subjected to principal component analysis (PCA) to assess their clustering tendency. The work is aimed at the identification of the most suitable model that is able to capture the information of the analyte and based on that, the model may be used for future E-Tongue applications. The results suggest that it is the linear equivalent circuit model which came out to be superior than the existing nonlinear and fractional-order model in terms of clustering propensity when PCA was performed with 20 samples of black tea. Therefore, the idea of considering the identified equivalent electric circuit parameters as characteristic features of an analyte is justified in this work.

articleTitle: Review of Voltage Limit and Transient Voltage Stability Criteria for Power System Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Voltage criteria in power systems during steady state and dynamic conditions are important for safe and secure grid operation and ensuring system planning with margin for security. This paper reviews and compares voltage stability criteria-specifically, voltage limit and transient voltage stability criteria across different countries and utilities used for power system planning and operation including India. Examining their implications for power system planning and operation, the study explores how criteria selection is influenced by regulatory frameworks, grid characteristics, and regional needs. By analyzing diverse approaches, the paper identifies commonalities and variations in voltage stability practices across the globe. It offers recommendations for tailoring criteria to specific contexts, emphasizing a balanced consideration of steady-state and transient stability. The research advances understanding of global voltage stability assessment methodologies, enabling better-informed decisions for ensuring grid reliability and sustainable energy delivery.

articleTitle: Potential Impact of Electric Vehicles on Indian Duck Curve
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The growth of the fleet of Electric Vehicles (EVs) globally has been happening exponentially because of its impact of decarbonizing the transportation sector. With the growing number of EV users, subsidized cost of the vehicle, and increasing awareness of the environment have led to increasing adoption of EVs which will further boost the number EVs in India. However, the increasing numbers of EV will lead to a change in the consumption pattern of the electricity consumers which will further reshape the load curve. This reshaping of the demand curve will lead to an issue of already existing duck curve. Again, the increasing adoption of solar in the distribution side of the grid will further deepen the belly of the duck curve. This paper studies the impact of increasing number of EV on the load curve and how it will impact the duck curve. Further, some solutions to solve the duck curve by modifying the EV charging pattern have also been discussed.

articleTitle: Experiences of Implementing Reverse Interlocking for Bus Bars with Multiple Infeed in Uganda
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Interlocked bus bar protection for a distribution system bus bar is a widely accepted concept. These interlocked bus bar protections are generally applied to low voltage systems with one incomer and multiple outgoing feeders. In this paper, the authors share their experiences while implementing the interlocked bus bar protection scheme in a system with bidirectional power flow in Uganda. The paper discusses in detail the implementation logics and the challenges faced during implementation due to the unique and complicated bus topology. We hope that the concepts discussed in this paper will serve as a reference for utility engineers when applying interlocked bus bar protection in a single bus bar with sectionalizers scheme and addressing the unique challenges associated with multiple infeeds to the bus bar.

articleTitle: Investigating the Effect of Outliers in Historical-Data on Grey Prediction Model for Power System State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper puts forth a closer look into the impact of having multiple outliers in the historical data, which are fed to the Grey Prediction Model named GM(1,1) for the purpose of predicting the value of current missing datum. The mentioned miss is majorly caused by sudden, momentary and unforeseen failures of measuring as well as telemetering equipment. Once the predicted datum is ready, it is able to aid the State Estimation (SE) of Power System. Weighted Least Squares (WLS) method is applied here as the SE technique.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Approach for Visual Testing of Web Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A novel ensemble approach for visual testing of web applications is proposed here, which aims to ensure the visual consistency and functionality of web applications across diverse configurations and user demands. The proposed approach integrates three models: a contour-based detection model, a YOLO-based granular analysis model, and a CNN-based design comparison model. The contour-based detection model identifies pixel-wise differences between the input and reference screenshots, the YOLO-based granular analysis model segments the screenshots into UI elements and locates the discrepancies, and the CNN-based design comparison model evaluates the aesthetic similarity between the input and reference screenshots. The proposed approach uses a comprehensive dataset of web application screenshots from Roboflow, comprising various UI elements and annotations. The paper presents empirical studies that show the superior performance and effectiveness of the proposed approach in detecting visual discrepancies and preserving user experience. Exploring the challenges and limitations of existing visual testing methods and tools, the study also outlines future directions to enhance the quality and reliability of web applications. Contributions to the advancement of automated testing techniques and tools for web development are made through this work.

articleTitle: Efficiency Augmentation Using SASTS and DASTS Under Instantly Varying Climatic Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Solar power generation stands as an immense, abundant, invaluable, and environmentally friendly non-conventional energy source. Given these remarkable attributes, the global community is actively engaged in seeking the most efficient and effective approaches for harnessing solar energy. A result of these endeavors is the advancement of stellar tracking systems, which optimize energy extraction through more sophisticated means. This study provides a concise overview of diverse stellar tracking mechanisms, with particular emphasis on lone-tracking and two-fold tracking systems The primary objective of this research is to compare and analyze three distinct methods of stellar tracking static, lone-axis, and two-fold axis, ultimately determining their suitability, effectiveness, and cost-efficiency across varying applications. The study involves assessing the incident stellar energy received by a stellar photovoltaic array of equivalent dimensions for each of the three methods over a defined period. Initially, energy generation is observed without the use of tracking systems, followed by experimentation with the entire setup incorporating tracking technology. The findings of the study reveal substantial disparities between the outputs obtained through the two approaches. This compellingly underscores the advantages of employing stellar tracking systems in enhancing energy generation.

articleTitle: Protection Strategies for an AC Microgrid: A Comprehensive Review
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The microgrid is evolved into a conventional distribution network as it enhances the reliability. However, the protection system requires more attention because of a micro-grid's bi-directional power flow and rising integration level. Hence, this study mainly focused on the issues, challenges, and solutions associated with the protection schemes for microgrids and the existing systems' research gaps. This paper reviews recent literature on the conventional and modern techniques- based protection schemes of the AC microgrids. Additionally, it also includes the current status of the research and the challenges under different operating conditions in the AC microgrid.

articleTitle: An Apple Detection Approach Based on Deep Learning Algorithm in Kashmir Orchards for Apple Harvester Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The apple industry in Kashmir, India, is one of the cornerstones of the region's economy. Efficient apple harvesting is crucial for both productivity and fruit quality. This paper presents an innovative approach for apple detection in Kashmir orchards using a deep learning algorithm, YOLOv8, integrated into a RealSense camera and an Apple Harvester Robot. The proposed method aims to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of the apple harvesting process, addressing the unique challenges posed by the varying lighting conditions, foliage, and diverse apple shapes and colors. YOLOv8, a state-of-the-art object detection model, is employed to detect apples in real-time. We fine-tuned the YOLOv8 model on a comprehensive dataset of annotated apple images from Kashmir orchards, ensuring that the model can effectively identify apples in different stages of maturity and amidst varying environmental conditions. Our approach not only detects apples but also localizes them with bounding boxes, providing precise information for the robot's manipulator to harvest the fruit with minimal damage. The algorithm we proposed has achieved an average of 91.2%. The recall and precision rates were 98% and 93.9% respectively. All the classifiers correctly predicted instances, in the dataset.

articleTitle: Face Detection with Landmark using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The advent of deep learning combined with computer vision has brought forth unparalleled advancements in facial detection and landmark identification. One pivotal player in this transformation has been the YOLO (You Only Look Once) series, setting new milestones in object detection methodologies. Our research is centered on harnessing the YOLOv8 model to optimize face detection processes. We incorporate the OpenCV library for image processing, enhancing detection fidelity through adjustable parameters like confidence and intersection over union (IoU) thresholds. A standout feature of our methodology is its innate ability to adjust to diverse image proportions. This is achieved by innovatively resizing and padding input images, which not only maintains consistency in detection but also augments accuracy. The proposed technique not only demarcates the face but also pinpoints facial landmarks, thus offering a comprehensive spatial map for each detected face. Preliminary results on benchmark datasets underscore the model's dual advantage of speed and precision. Our approach promises not only improved face detection but also paves the way for its amalgamation into expansive facial recognition and analytic platforms.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Synchrophasor Estimation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The synchrophasor measurement is an evolving technology for power system supervision and control. It's suitable for monitoring current scenario of power system parameters. The most important element when determining the accuracy of the synchrophasor is the phasor estimate technique. This paper discusses the modern phasor estimation with the performance requirement. Further, it presents a comprehensive review of the various phasor estimation technique with their performance improvements and limitations. It also indicates the gaps in the attainment of performance requirements in existing techniques and the scope for future research work.

articleTitle: Higher Order Dynamic Mode Decomposition for Robust Parameter Estimation in Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The stability, effectiveness, and high-quality operation of the electrical system are maintained through the monitoring of fundamental parameters like frequency and amplitude. The current research provides a data-driven hybrid technique for the extraction of fundamental parameters using the Higher-order dynamic mode decomposition (HODMD) algorithm in smart grid. HODMD's capacity to account for non-linearities enables it to produce accurate representations of the underlying dynamics, resulting in better model estimation. Thus, HODMD is an appropriate method for power quality analysis due to its capacity to analyze multidimensional data and non-uniformly sampled data. In this work, the potential of HODMD is examined for the estimation of fundamental frequency, amplitude, and the existence of disturbance components, such as harmonics. In the proposed methodology, HODMD modes are computed using the low-rank approximation and then extracted the amplitude and frequency information from the data. The hyper parameters of the proposed methodology are properly tuned to get an accurate estimate of the underlying parameters. The optimistic results on various synthetic and real-time scenarios indicate that the proposed methodology can be utilized to determine the power system frequency and amplitude in general periodic and quasi-periodic dynamics.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Performance of Resumable Load Data Compression Algorithm (RLDA) for Distribution Voltage and Frequency Monitoring Data
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Data acquisition is a crucial for monitoring power system and analysing the system conditions in a precise manner. It is often responsible for producing an enormous volume of information and therefore compression of such information can be useful for reducing the volume of information considerably. Resumable Load Data Compression Algorithm (RLDA) developed originally for compressing load profile data, is a differential coding based lossless algorithm which can be an alternative for compressing the slow varying monitoring data sets. Therefore, the performance of RLDA is investigated for compressing the practical voltage and frequency datasets to check its compatibility with the developed works before attempting its implementation at the hardware level. The respective routines were developed in the MATLAB environment and the analysis is performed with practical voltage and frequency datasets. A voltage measurement system is developed in the laboratory of NIT Sikkim for acquiring the practical distribution voltage datasets at the initial level of the work. From the obtained results, it is clear that the volume of information reduces by more than 60% for the majority of data sets. Several scopes of improvement are identified for the improvement of the work based on which conclusion is drawn.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Jamming and Spoofing Attack on GNSS Signals Using Subspace Projection
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The precision, position, and timing information provided by Global Positioning System (GPS) technology is essential for various commercial and military applications, including navigation systems for smartwatches, ships, drones, and autonomous vehicles. However, GPS technology is vulnerable to spoofing and jamming attacks due to its open design, which can have significant consequences. To mitigate the vulnerability of GPS technology to spoofing and jamming attacks, this paper proposes a subspace projection-based mitigation scheme. The scheme involves a systematic approach in which the line signal is projected to an orthogonal subspace and used in the conventional Direction of Arrival estimation using Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in mitigating these attacks.

articleTitle: Adversity Analysis of Cyber-attacks on Load Frequency Control of Hybrid Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Ever increasing power demand and focus on green energy has increased the use of renewable energy resources (RES) leading towards low inertia of microgrid that causes frequency oscillations and may make the microgrid unstable. The frequency regulation activities are maintained by the load frequency control (LFC) in a power system or microgrid. LFC involves data to be sensed at a remote location of power system and then this measured data is communicated over a distance to the controller terminals. The communication network is prone to attacks/threats. So, the frequency deviation for cyber-attack affects all other interconnected areas, and thus threatens the stability of the entire network. This paper focuses on cyber security issues in LFC due to the effect of different cyber-attacks. The sensitivity evaluation is executed to comprehend the feasible threats causing stability failure, and their origin. Variety of attacks, viz. denial of service attack (DoS), false data injection (FDI) attack, resonance attack, are investigated on a multi-source hybrid microgrid. Different type of FDI attacks such as scaling attack, ramp attack, pulse attack and random attack are implemented in this paper. Moreover, multiple nonlinearities like generation rate constraints, boiler dynamics and governor dead band are included in the system model so that the stability of the microgrid can be examined for more realistic situation.

articleTitle: Significance of Convolutional Neural Network in View of Lip Reading for Speech-Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: One way to understand what another person is saying is by lip reading. This is done by observing the speaker's lips movements and determining the words being spoken. One of the key problems with lip reading methods is visual uncertainty, making it difficult to implement in practice. When homophones have similar or nearly identical lip movement, this occurs at the word level. ([p], [m], [b] are all examples). One of the primary factors behind this effort is the intention to aid those who struggle with speech problems. Many people throughout the globe have difficulties communicating because of speech impediments, but visual speech recognition has the potential to change that. In the past ten years, as deep learning has developed, there has been a steady increase in the requirement for effective speech-to-text systems. Intelligent devices that can read lips are called lip reading systems. In order to convert lip movement into text, it is necessary to identify the face, find the lips, identify the characteristics, and then train the classifier to detect lip movement. This article presents an extensive examination of the latest advancements in deep learning model-based Visual speech recognition (VSR). The emphasis is on addressing data problems, task-specific complexities like homophones and absence of context, and providing existing results. Progress in these areas will accelerate the implementation of the silent speech interface from concept to reality. In addition to that, we also summarised the statistical results of standard datasets of VSR.

articleTitle: A Survey on the Development of Wireless Sensor Network Challenges Using ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A wireless sensor network is a network that consists of a number of sensor nodes that are used to communicate wirelessly. These nodes are used to continuously monitor changes in the environment in a sensing area that are due to external factors, system design hardware, etc. Due to the limited power of wireless sensor networks and the constantly shifting topology of the network, attempts Common techniques for security, such as cryptography and key management, are useless. Machine learning(ML) algorithms can combine surveillance and intelligence-based decisions to deliver safety measures in this kind of system are one of the suggested methods. This information is given to a central processing area, which is a base station connected to the internet, through which a user can observe. WSN is a network that is an enabler for IOT Technology. In this review paper, we analyze over a two-decade time period in WSN issues or challenges faced, which can be reduced using different algorithms of machine learning. In this survey paper, some of the issues faced by WSN are Security, Routing, Clustering, Localization, Fault detection, Medium Access Control (MAC) protocols, etc., so by using ML algorithms, they are evaluated against the corresponding problems. Thus, this review paper provides an overall idea of ML algorithms for different issues faced by WSN.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Charging Infrastructure for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) are rising as one of the favourable strategies to overcome the increasing environmental concerns due to over-dependence on fossil fuels, emissions, and energy insufficiency. This work aims to design and develop a software framework to contribute to the EV charging infrastructure. The proposed work includes (1) creating front-end software for charging station operators and owners for managing and operating charging points, (2) developing cloud-based intelligent models for region prediction, price prediction, station filtering, and slot booking, (3) designing slot scheduling algorithms for optimal utilization of the charging station. Python and software tools like Streamlit, SQL, and Flask facilitate the implementation of the front-end software, database, and computational algorithms. The web application, built using the Streamlit Python framework, acts as the user interface for all stakeholders. The work utilizes the Linear Search Algorithm and the Binary Search Algorithm to filter stations based on the user requirements, such as distance and price range, which users indicate through the web application. The Gradient Boosting approach gives good results for region prediction for the chosen dataset of EV charging stations. In this work, a priority scheduling approach considering the time-of-use price achieves EV charging slot allocation. The software framework provides a comprehensive electric vehicle charging infrastructure where users can easily find the best charging station and reserve a spot for charging. The work's future extension can include the addition of functionalities for Vehicle-to-vehicle and Vehicle-to-grid.

articleTitle: Robotic Terrain Classification with Loss Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Locomotion mechanics of legged robots are suitable when pacing through difficult terrains. Recognising terrains for such robots are important to fully yoke the versatility of their movements. Consequently, robotic terrain classification becomes significant to classify terrains in real time with high accuracy. The conventional classifiers suffer from overfitting problem, low accuracy problem, high variance problem, and not suitable for live dataset. On the other hand, classifying a growing dataset is difficult for convolution based terrain classification. Supervised recurrent models are also not practical for this classification. Further, the existing recurrent architectures are still evolving to improve accuracy of terrain classification based on live variable-length sensory data collected from legged robots. This paper proposes a new semi-supervised method for terrain classification of legged robots, avoiding preprocessing of long variable-length dataset. The proposed method has a stacked Long Short-Term Memory architecture, including a new loss regularization. The proposed method solves the existing problems and improves accuracy. Comparison with the existing architectures show the improvements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Policies in India Emphasizing Towards Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Worldwide, the requirement and necessities of re-newable energy has grown over the span of years because of tremendous increment of carbon dioxide emissions and its adverse effect on environment. In 2022, globally CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions has shown a growth of about 5.7% because of rapid increment in electricity consumption. An emissions are completely responsible to electrical energy utilisation. 79 % of historical carbon emissions were caused by wealthy countries rather than less developed nations. In order to examine the effectiveness of current solar energy strategies in India and compare it to South Asian countries, this article gives a survey of solar energy policies implemented in India since independence. Moreover, this paper compares the strategies between developed and under developed countries policies on effective implementation of renewables into power sector in order to reduce emissions and to protect enviornment.
